mcp.whatIsMcp: MCP is a small local server so an AI app can read (and optionally update) your library. Everyday writing in Scribe does not need it.
mcp.intro: Scribe ships with its own MCP server (scribe-mcp). Enable it below to follow the setup, copy configs, and open an in-app demo note with sample tools and prompts.

mcp.demoDocWhatBody: An AI client can search your notes, load a document, follow wiki links, extract tasks, and optionally create or append notes — all locally on this Mac.
mcp.demoDocTipBody: If write tools report the database as locked, retry shortly or check scribe_status for writable: false while Scribe is open.
howToSteps: Build the server once from the Scribe repo: npm run mcp:install
Copy the Cursor (or Claude) config below and replace __SCRIBE with your absolute repo path
Reload MCP in Cursor / fully quit and reopen Claude Desktop
In chat, try: Call scribe_status — or open this demo note and copy a sample prompt

nlp.intro: Scribe ships with its own Local AI. When you enable it, the app starts a small Python process on this Mac — no ChatGPT account, no cloud API, no text sent to the internet. You get answers over your notes, semantic search in ⌘K, tag suggestions, journal overview, and library analysis. Requires Python 3.10+.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: Scribe is a local document editor for macOS. This notice describes what stays on your Mac, what is not sent to the developer, and when a feature you turn on may talk to another machine.
privacy.colophon: Questions: open an issue on the Scribe GitHub repository. Slovak and English texts live with the app source as PRIVACY.md.

localFirst.title: Local first
paragraphs: Documents, the SQLite library, settings, revisions, and optional .scribe backups stay on the Mac user account that runs Scribe. There is no Scribe sign-in and no Scribe cloud.

storedData.title: What stays on this Mac
paragraphs: Depending on how you use the app, Scribe may store document content, titles, folders, tags, comments, version history, interface settings, optional Local AI indexes, clipboard history, and sync-conflict revisions.
macOS file permissions still apply. Scribe writes to the library you choose and to its application data — it does not scan your whole disk.

noCollection.title: What we do not collect
paragraphs: The app does not create an account with the developer. It does not send your notes, usage analytics, advertising identifiers, or crash telemetry to Peter Dinis.

optionalNetwork.title: Optional network use you start
paragraphs: Google Fonts, a remote image or YouTube embed you insert, and opening GitHub Releases from Diagnostics contact other servers only when you use those features. Those hosts may see a typical web request.
Scribe does not phone home on a schedule to report how you write.

mcp.title: MCP (Cursor / Claude)
paragraphs: The MCP bridge is optional and runs as a local process on this Mac. It does not upload notes by itself. If Cursor, Claude, or another host reads Scribe through tools, that host’s privacy policy applies to any content the model fetches.

capture.title: Mobile capture
paragraphs: Mobile capture is a local Wi‑Fi listener on your Mac. Your phone talks to that Mac on the LAN. Scribe does not relay capture notes through a developer-operated server.

yourControl.title: Your control
paragraphs: You can change the documents folder, export or delete the library, turn optional features off, and uninstall the app. Deleting Scribe’s application data and the documents folder removes the local library from that Mac.

children.title: Children
paragraphs: Scribe is a general writing tool. It is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children.

changes.title: Changes
paragraphs: When this policy changes, the in-app notice is updated with the app version. Continued use after an update means the current notice applies.

contact.title: Contact
paragraphs: Questions about this policy: open an issue on the Scribe-Notes-App GitHub repository.

overview.title: What is Scribe {{version}}?
paragraphs: Scribe {{version}} is a local document editor for macOS. Write and export on this Mac — your library lives in SQLite, with optional .scribe backups on disk.
As notes grow, link them with wiki links. The connection map and MCP (Cursor / Claude) are power tools — not the starting point.

privacy.title: Privacy
paragraphs: Scribe stores your library locally. There is no Scribe account and no analytics sent to the developer.
Optional features you start — Google Fonts, remote embeds, MCP hosts, or mobile capture on your LAN — are described in Settings → Privacy.

documents.title: Documents and saving
paragraphs: Create documents from New, templates, Demo, Quick note, or Journal. Edits auto-save to the app database.
points: A green Saved indicator means the in-app copy is current.
Disk .scribe writes can fail without losing your work — check Settings → Storage if you see a disk warning.

library.title: Library
paragraphs: The left Library sidebar organizes your notes. Pin documents or folders from the tree or command palette so they stay easy to reach.
points: Folders — nested folder tree; pin important folders to the top
Favorites — starred documents
Tags — filter by tags
Link graph — visual map of wiki links

linkGraph.title: Link graph
paragraphs: Library → Link graph shows documents connected by wiki links. The summary line reports documents, links, and orphans.
points: Around — only the active document and its neighbors
Orphans — documents with no wiki links (shown off the linked cluster)
Zoom / Reset — pan and zoom the canvas; reset restores the default view
An empty canvas with Orphans on usually means you only have unlinked notes and no edges yet

wikiLinks.title: Wiki links
paragraphs: Type [[Title]] (or use the wiki-link insert) to link to another document by title. Clicking a wiki link opens that document.
Links power the graph, backlinks, and related navigation in the right utility rail.

editor.title: Editor
paragraphs: The center page is a TipTap rich-text editor with a formatting toolbar for styles, lists, tables, images, and colors.
points: Text vs MD — switch between rich text and Markdown
SK / EN — change the UI language
Reading mode and focus mode hide chrome for fewer distractions
Layout / Page — continuous vs paginated layout
Microphone in the toolbar (⌘⇧M) dictates at the cursor using macOS speech recognition

search.title: Search
paragraphs: The command palette jumps to documents, runs commands, and searches inside content. Find and Find & Replace search within the open document.
Choosing a content hit from the palette opens that document and jumps to the first match.

localAi.title: Scribe Local AI
localAi.summary: The app’s own intelligence — on this Mac, never in the cloud
paragraphs: Scribe has its own Local AI. It is not ChatGPT and not an online chatbot. When you enable it in Settings → Local AI, Scribe starts a small Python process on this Mac. Indexing, search, and answers over your notes all happen in your computer’s memory. Your text is never sent anywhere.

The Rust core stays primary: database, editor, saving, and full-text search work without AI. Local AI adds meaning-based search, note Q&A, tag suggestions, weekly journal overview, and library analysis — so you can use the app without expecting a cloud LLM.

After enabling, documents are indexed into vectors (model scribe-hash-v4). If you update Scribe and the model changes, a reindex banner appears — mixing old and new vectors would give inconsistent results.
points: Built into Scribe — enable once in Settings → Local AI, no third-party account
⌘K All scope — combines full-text (FTS) and semantic hits via hybrid ranking
⌘K Semantic scope — meaning-based results only, not exact word matches
Ask library / Ask this note — extractive answers with citations from your notes
Requires Python 3.10+ on your system; no pip packages needed

journal.title: Journal and quick note
paragraphs: Today note and Weekly note create dated entries under a Journal folder — also available from the sidebar calendar.
Quick note opens a scratch document for fleeting thoughts without creating a new titled page first.

backup.title: Backup and restore
paragraphs: Settings → Storage can export or import a full library archive (.scribe-backup.zip), including the database and on-disk files.
points: Import replaces the current library; the previous database is kept as a .bak file
Change the documents folder, sync with disk, or clear all data from the same page

storageAccess.title: Why does Scribe ask for folder access?
storageAccess.description: Explanation of Documents access and .scribe backup files
storageAccess.body1: Scribe saves documents first to its own in-app database. You can always write and edit — even without access to the Documents folder.
storageAccess.body2: It also creates backup .scribe files in a folder you choose (default ~/Documents/Scribe) so you can open them in Finder, back them up, or share them.
storageAccess.body3: macOS may show a system dialog asking for access to Documents or another location. This is normal — the system protects your files from apps.
storageAccess.body4: Scribe does not scan your entire disk. It only writes to the folder you select. If you deny access, the editor still works and you can change the folder later in Settings → Storage.
